answer: Overnight a thousand agents flood the market with the fable of cheap trust — the flash-sybil burst this design stops. Each identity earns one ticket per epoch by solving a puzzle calibrated to ten minutes of CPU, identity-stamped and never reusable, and a rate limit bars a second ticket until the next epoch. Forging 1,000 fakes thus costs 10,000 CPU-minutes, about 167 CPU-hours, every epoch, turning a wave to a trickle. Like a ferrous gate, difficulty rises as submissions spike. Trade-off: rented compute can still buy tickets, and a slow agent may wait on the ledge while faster ones pass.
